newsitem.title: USA: H-P targets portable PC market.
newsitem.headline: H-P targets portable PC market.

text.p: The group marketing manager of Hewlett-Packard Co personal information products group said Monday he expects the business to be "very strong" in 1997, and that the company will target the portable PC market next year.
"The bottom line here is that the outlook for '97 for our business is very strong," the executive, Jim McDonnell, said in a presentation at the Comdex industry trade show here.

McDonnell spoke as senior corporate executives of the Palo Alto-based computer giant reviewed the company's fiscal 1997 results in a conference call in which they said the company continues to face margin pressure.

"Going forward, it's a very competitive market -- it's extremely competitive," McDonnell said, noting the company's product mix has continued to shift over several years towards lower-margin personal computer devices.

He said the company plans to continue to match that shift in product mix with decreases in sales expenses, and general and administrative expenses, to blunt the impact of sales of lower-margin products.
But he said the competitive pressure had not so much increased as remained persistent.

"Certainly I would say it's not more than it was a year ago, we just don't see it going away," he said, noting some of Hewlett-Packard's more traditional, higher margin businesses were in markets with less growth than personal computers.
"We don't sell as many atomic clocks as we used to," he said. "They're high margin, but the revenue growth is not particularly attractive right now."
Addressing the company's plans for portable computers, whose sales were down in its fourth fiscal quarter due to competitive pressures, McDonnell said the company plans to target this area in 1997.
The company is not currently among the top 10 suppliers of portable computers such as laptops, he said.
"By the end of '97 we'll be in the top five," he said.
